knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.1.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) How do you compare two estimators using MSE? (2) When can an unbiased estimator lose to a biased one on MSE? (3) What claim must you refuse about asymptotics today?
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Prefer the estimator with smaller MSE (CMP examples). A biased estimator can have smaller MSE than an unbiased one if variance reduction outweighs squared bias. Asymptotic MLE laws are tomorrow. Not today's LO.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.1.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Two estimators of θ: θ̂₁ is unbiased with Var=2/n; θ̂₂ has Bias=0.5/√n and Var=0.5/n. (1) Compare them using MSE. Which do you prefer for large n? (2) Refuse: 'Bias and MSE are defined, so comparison is automatic without computing either estimator's MSE.'
knowledge_checks.body: Explicit MSE comparison of two estimators; refuse definition-as-comparison.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Estimator comparison under this LO is an explicit MSE/bias calculation, not property-definition recall.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) MSE₁=2/n; MSE₂=(0.5/√n)² + 0.5/n = 0.25/n + 0.5/n = 0.75/n. Prefer θ̂₂ on MSE (0.75/n < 2/n). (2) Refuse: comparison requires an explicit MSE (or bias) comparison of the named estimators. Definitions alone are not a comparison.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Stopping at property definitions without comparing the two estimators numerically.
success_criteria: Computes both MSEs and states a preference.
Refuses treating definitions as an automatic comparison.
